title: Ġgantija temples
description: Farmers on Gozo raise two stone temples that are among the oldest free-standing buildings in the world.

title: Rome takes Malta
description: At the start of the Second Punic War a Roman fleet takes the islands from Carthage.

title: Shipwreck of Paul
description: According to the Acts of the Apostles, Paul is wrecked on the island on his way to Rome; Maltese tradition dates its Christianity from this.

title: Aghlabid conquest
description: An Arab army from Sicily takes and destroys the Byzantine city; Arab rule leaves the island its language.

title: Norman invasion
description: Roger I of Sicily lands and makes the Muslim rulers his tributaries, tying Malta to Sicily for four centuries.

title: Battle of Malta
description: An Aragonese fleet under Roger of Lauria destroys an Angevin fleet in the harbour during the War of the Sicilian Vespers.

title: Knights Hospitaller given Malta
description: Emperor Charles V grants the islands to the Order of St John, homeless since the loss of Rhodes, for the yearly rent of a falcon.

title: Sack of Gozo
description: An Ottoman fleet carries off almost the whole population of Gozo into slavery.

title: Great Siege of Malta
description: The knights and the Maltese hold out for nearly four months against an Ottoman army until relief comes from Sicily.

title: Valletta founded
description: Grand Master Jean de Valette lays the first stone of a fortified city on the headland the Ottomans had used.

title: French invasion
description: Bonaparte, on his way to Egypt, takes the islands and ends the rule of the knights.

title: French garrison surrenders
description: After a Maltese rising and a two-year blockade the French give up Valletta to the British.

title: Treaty of Paris confirms British rule
description: The peace with France recognises Malta as a British possession, and it becomes the main base of the Mediterranean Fleet.

title: Sette Giugno riots
description: British troops fire on crowds protesting at the price of bread, killing four; self-government follows in 1921.

title: Siege of Malta
description: Italian and German aircraft bomb the island for over two years to stop it from cutting the supply line to North Africa.

title: George Cross awarded to Malta
description: George VI awards the medal to the whole island; it is on the flag to this day.

title: Operation Pedestal
description: Five ships of a convoy of fourteen, among them the tanker Ohio, reach the starving island.

title: Independence
description: Malta becomes independent of Britain, with the queen as head of state.

title: Republic
description: Malta becomes a republic within the Commonwealth, with Anthony Mamo as its first president.

title: Last British forces leave
description: The military agreement with Britain runs out and, for the first time in its recorded history, no foreign troops are based on the island.

title: Malta Summit
description: George Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev meet on a ship in the bay weeks after the fall of the Berlin Wall, a meeting often taken as the end of the Cold War.

title: Malta joins the European Union
description: Malta enters the European Union as its smallest member.

title: Euro adopted
description: The euro replaces the Maltese lira.

title: Murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia
description: A car bomb kills the journalist who had reported on corruption, and the inquiry later brings down the prime minister.
